lead.hed: Defense News: Navy RFI wants carrier drones at $30 million, five tons of weapons
lead.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: the Navy’s Aug. 31 request for information asks industry for carrier-based Collaborative Combat Aircraft that can carry up to five tons of weapons, four 2,500-pound stores externally, and cost no more than $30 million each. Responses are due Sept. 18. The service wants two prototypes that can qualify ashore and on a carrier within three years. An RFI is a shopping list, not a contract award.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo · DVIDS 9805182 · PUBLIC DOMAIN · MH-60R Sea Hawk launches from USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72), June 29, 2026, Arabian Sea. Caption must say June file photo, not today’s RFI.
lead.image_note: Official U.S. Navy DVIDS still of carrier flight operations — same-subject class as the Navy CCA carrier-drone RFI. Not a brand tile.

political.hed: USNI: Japan’s FY2027 request hits a record $55.6 billion for unmanned and long-range strike
political.insight: USNI News, Tuesday afternoon: Tokyo’s Ministry of Defense budget request for fiscal 2027 puts a record $55.6 billion toward unmanned systems and long-range strike, with ministry concept art of stand-off missiles from multiple platforms. A request is not appropriated cash. Diet action still decides what gets bought.

political.hed: USNI: Marines staged a Hornet maritime-strike package off Japan
political.insight: USNI News, Tuesday: ten F/A-18 Hornets from Marine Fighter Attack Squadron 232 launched last month from Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni with an anti-ship missile loadout. The item is a demonstration of maritime strike, not a claim of combat employment.

political.hed: WORLD: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns after friction with Hegseth
political.insight: WORLD, Tuesday, citing the Wall Street Journal and Associated Press: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll planned to step down after about 18 months, following disagreements with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. WORLD notes he had not issued a formal statement at publish time. A resignation report is not a named successor.

tech.hed: USNI: GAO warns 15 attack boats face idle time through 2030
tech.insight: USNI News, Tuesday, on a GAO report: without mitigation, 15 attack submarines will enter inactive idle time from fiscal 2026 through 2030 — more than 14,000 idle days and $3.1 billion in operating costs while those hulls sit. The report is a warning on maintenance capacity, not a claim the boats are already laid up.

tech.hed: Defense News: Pentagon frameworks aim to triple Patriot and quadruple THAAD output
tech.insight: Defense News, Monday: the Pentagon signed framework agreements with Lockheed Martin and General Dynamics to surge interceptor production, including tripling Patriot output and quadrupling THAAD interceptors. Frameworks set targets; they are not finished missiles on the ramp.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: the Constitution is not as godless as postliberals say
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Monday: a review argues the American Constitution is not as “godless” as postliberal critics claim, but that the people still have to sustain spiritual capital for it to work. The piece is an argument about founding order, not a court ruling.

culture.hed: WORLD: Colorado’s Catholic preschool funding fight is at the Supreme Court
culture.insight: WORLD Legal Docket: Colorado requires Catholic preschools that take state money to set aside religious standards even as secular providers may tailor enrollment. WORLD frames it as a First Amendment conflict now headed to the Court. Oral argument is still ahead.
